problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=0.7x-0.35xy \\ {y}^{′}=-0.4y+2xy\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.$\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0.2,\,2]^{T},$ we get

| $J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  | $\,.$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |

$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are 
{{field-5}}.

$\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is
{{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=0.7x-0.35xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-0.4y+2xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(0.7x-0.35xy)=0.7-0.35y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(0.7x-0.35xy)=-0.35x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-0.4y+2xy)=2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-0.4y+2xy)=-0.4+2x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}0.7-0.35y & -0.35x \\ 2y & -0.4+2x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0.2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}0.7-0.35(2) & -0.35(0.2) \\ 2(2) & -0.4+2(0.2)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -0.07 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & -0.07 \\ 4 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )(-\lambda )-4\cdot (-0.07) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+0.28 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=\pm 0.2\sqrt{7}\,\text{i}.$ Since the eigenvalues are purely imaginary, our equilibrium is $\text{a stable}$ $\text{center}.$

**Note:**
For the Lotka-Volterra model (as in this problem), it is safe to classify the nonzero equilibrium as a center when the linearization has purely imaginary eigenvalues. 

**Watch out!** 
In contrast, for a general nonlinear system, the Jacobian test alone is inconclusive (additional analysis is required to determine whether the equilibrium is a true center or a spiral sink/source).
